base-skip-to-content: Accessibility skip link at the top of every page; jumps keyboard/screen-reader users past the header to the main content. Rendered before the message catalogue loads, so the server stamps it into the page rather than the app looking it up.
base-admin-badge: Small badge shown in the header on admin pages, indicating admin mode. Keep short.
base-log-out: Header button that signs the user out. Lowercase to match the compact header style.
base-admin-link: Header link to the admin dashboard, shown only to administrators. Lowercase to match the header style.
base-log-in: Header link to sign in (Wikimedia OAuth). Lowercase to match the header style.
base-dismiss: Accessible label (aria-label) for the × button that closes a toast/notification.
common-opens-in-new-tab: Visually-hidden suffix appended to links that open a new browser tab, for screen-reader users. Note the leading space.
home-timeline-aria: Accessible label for the small progress timeline on a consultation card showing which phase the consultation has reached.
home-phase-explore:
Name of the first consultation phase (voting on statements). Also used in the phase legend and timeline.
{{Identical|Explore}}
home-phase-arguments:
Name of the arguments/argument-mapping phase. Used in the phase legend and timeline.
{{Identical|Arguments}}
home-phase-informed-vote:
Name of the informed opinion phase, a second round of responses held after the arguments. Used in the phase legend and timeline.
{{Identical|Informed opinion}}
home-phase-report:
Name of the final report/results phase. Used in the phase legend.
{{Identical|Report}}
home-phase-optin-id: Last step in the timeline on a consultation card: after the consultation closes, participants may link their Wikimedia username to their pseudonym for a limited period.
home-outputs-aria: Accessible label for the grid of output symbols (report, data, etc.) on a consultation card.
home-chip-to-vote: Chip on a consultation card. $1 is the number of statements the user still has to respond to.
home-chip-next:
Chip on a consultation card announcing its next scheduled phase change, e.g. "Next: Informed opinion 1 Oct 2026, 12:00". Parameters:
* $1 - the name of the next phase, e.g. {{msg-proto|phase-label-informed_voting}}
* $2 - the date and time, a <nowiki><time></nowiki> element formatted in the chosen language and the reader's timezone, with {{msg-proto|conv-scheduled-tz-title}} as its tooltip
The longer notice inside a consultation is {{msg-proto|conv-scheduled-transition}}.
home-chip-reveal-today: Chip on a consultation card warning that today is the last day participants can link their Wikimedia username to their pseudonym.
home-chip-reveal-days: Chip on a consultation card warning how long participants can still link their Wikimedia username to their pseudonym. $1 is a number of days; 'd' abbreviates 'days'.
home-chip-reveal-opens: Chip on a consultation card noting when participants will be able to link their Wikimedia username to their pseudonym. $1 is a number of days; 'd' abbreviates 'days'.
home-banner-prototype: Banner at the top of the landing page and the consultation list. $1 is a link labelled {{msg-proto|home-banner-open-issue}} that opens the issue tracker in a new tab.
home-banner-open-issue: Link text in the prototype banner to report a bug (opens the GitHub issue tracker).
home-hero-heading: Main heading on the signed-out landing page. The product's value proposition.
home-hero-body: First line of the landing page's explanation, above {{msg-proto|home-hero-detail}}. Its own paragraph.
home-hero-detail: Second paragraph of the landing page's explanation, under {{msg-proto|home-hero-body}}: what a participant does, and what the consultation process shows them.
home-login-wikimedia: Label on the button that starts Wikimedia OAuth login.
home-dev-badge: Label for the local-development-only login shortcuts. Only visible in dev mode.
home-dev-login-as: title attribute (tooltip) on a dev login shortcut. $1 is a username. Dev-only.
home-open-consultations: Section heading listing publicly-open consultations to signed-out visitors.
home-count-total: Count shown next to a section heading. $1 is the number of items.
home-card-join-aria: Accessible label for a consultation card link. $1 is the consultation title.
home-action-join: Call-to-action on a consultation card to join it. The arrow is decorative. Rendered in capitals by CSS; write it in sentence case.
home-action-continue: Call-to-action on a consultation card the user has already joined. The arrow is decorative. Rendered in capitals by CSS; write it in sentence case.
home-action-view: Call-to-action on a consultation card with nothing for the user to do: caught up, inactive or closed. Rendered in capitals by CSS; the arrow is decorative.
home-action-admin: Call-to-action to open the admin panel for a consultation the user moderates. The arrow is decorative. Rendered in capitals by CSS; write it in sentence case.
home-flow-alt: alt text for the diagram illustrating how a Proto consultation flows through its phases.
flow-title: Title of the flow diagram on the consultation list, which shows the three rounds and what each one produces. The diagram is a drawing with its English inside it, so it still shows English until it is rebuilt; translations are collected now so they are ready when it is.
flow-subtitle: Subtitle under {{msg-proto|flow-title}} in the flow diagram: what the process is for. The diagram is a drawing with its English inside it, so it still shows English until it is rebuilt; translations are collected now so they are ready when it is.
flow-learn-label:
Small label above the result of each round in the flow diagram, e.g. above {{msg-proto|flow-explore-learn}}. Rendered in capitals; write it in sentence case.
{{Identical|What we learn}} The diagram is a drawing with its English inside it, so it still shows English until it is rebuilt; translations are collected now so they are ready when it is.
flow-explore-title: Heading of the first round in the flow diagram. The round itself is {{msg-proto|phase-label-submission}}. The diagram is a drawing with its English inside it, so it still shows English until it is rebuilt; translations are collected now so they are ready when it is.
flow-explore-body: What a participant does in the first round, under {{msg-proto|flow-explore-title}} in the flow diagram. The diagram is a drawing with its English inside it, so it still shows English until it is rebuilt; translations are collected now so they are ready when it is.
flow-explore-learn: What the first round produces, shown under {{msg-proto|flow-learn-label}} in the flow diagram. Two lines in the drawing; write it as one sentence. The diagram is a drawing with its English inside it, so it still shows English until it is rebuilt; translations are collected now so they are ready when it is.
flow-arguments-title: Heading of the second round in the flow diagram. The round itself is {{msg-proto|phase-label-argument_mapping}}. The diagram is a drawing with its English inside it, so it still shows English until it is rebuilt; translations are collected now so they are ready when it is.
flow-arguments-body: What a participant does in the second round, under {{msg-proto|flow-arguments-title}} in the flow diagram. The diagram is a drawing with its English inside it, so it still shows English until it is rebuilt; translations are collected now so they are ready when it is.
flow-arguments-learn: What the second round produces, shown under {{msg-proto|flow-learn-label}} in the flow diagram. The diagram is a drawing with its English inside it, so it still shows English until it is rebuilt; translations are collected now so they are ready when it is.
flow-informed-title: Heading of the third round in the flow diagram. The round itself is {{msg-proto|phase-label-informed_voting}}. The diagram is a drawing with its English inside it, so it still shows English until it is rebuilt; translations are collected now so they are ready when it is.
flow-informed-body: What a participant does in the third round, under {{msg-proto|flow-informed-title}} in the flow diagram. The diagram is a drawing with its English inside it, so it still shows English until it is rebuilt; translations are collected now so they are ready when it is.
flow-informed-learn: What the third round produces, shown under {{msg-proto|flow-learn-label}} in the flow diagram. The diagram is a drawing with its English inside it, so it still shows English until it is rebuilt; translations are collected now so they are ready when it is.
flow-outcome: The outcome at the end of the flow diagram, after the three rounds. The diagram is a drawing with its English inside it, so it still shows English until it is rebuilt; translations are collected now so they are ready when it is.
home-phase-legend-aria: Accessible label for the phase-journey legend diagram.
home-view-mode-aria: Accessible label for the toggle switching between the user's own consultations and browsing all.
home-mode-yours: Toggle button showing the consultations the signed-in user has joined.
home-mode-browse: Toggle button to browse all consultations open to the user.
home-heading:
Visually hidden page heading of the consultation list, for screen readers.
{{Identical|Consultations}}
home-section-closed:
Section heading for the user's closed consultations.
{{Identical|Closed}}
home-section-open-to-you: Section heading for consultations the user may join but has not yet.
home-section-moderate: Section heading listing consultations the user moderates/administers.
home-section-needs-attention: Section heading for the user's consultations where there is something for them to do, such as statements left to vote on. Rendered in capitals by CSS; write it in sentence case.
home-section-caught-up: Section heading for the reader's consultations where they have responded to every statement available so far. Rendered in capitals by CSS; write it in sentence case. "Done for now" rather than "caught up", which is English idiom that does not translate.
home-section-inactive: Section heading for the user's consultations that are paused, or in a phase with nothing for participants to do. Rendered in capitals by CSS; write it in sentence case.
home-card-aria-pseudonym: Fragment appended to a card's accessible label naming the user's pseudonym in that consultation. $1 is the pseudonym.
home-card-aria-remaining: Fragment appended to a card's accessible label with how many statements are still left for the user to respond to. $1 is a number.
home-card-aria-continue: Fragment appended to an active card's accessible label indicating the action is to continue.
home-card-aria-closed: Fragment appended to a closed card's accessible label indicating it is closed.
home-card-aria-caught-up: Fragment appended to the accessible label of a consultation card in the {{msg-proto|home-section-caught-up}} section. Other fragments may precede it, such as {{msg-proto|home-card-aria-pseudonym}}; the dash separates it from them.
home-card-aria-inactive: Fragment appended to the accessible label of a consultation card in the {{msg-proto|home-section-inactive}} section. "Inactive" describes the consultation.
home-card-badge-closed:
Small badge marking a consultation as closed.
{{Identical|closed}}
home-card-badge-caught-up: Small badge on a consultation card: the reader has responded to every statement available so far, and more may appear later. Describes the reader's state in that consultation, not the consultation's.
home-card-badge-paused: Small badge on a consultation card: an organizer has paused the consultation. Describes the consultation.
home-card-badge-waiting: Small badge on a consultation card: the consultation is between phases, with nothing for participants to do until the next one opens. Describes the consultation.
home-card-view-aria: Accessible label for a moderated consultation's title link. $1 is the title.
home-card-admin-aria: Accessible label for the admin-panel link on a moderated consultation. $1 is the title.
home-empty-none-joined: Shown in the Your consultations tab when the reader has joined nothing. "New consultations" is {{msg-proto|home-mode-browse}}, the other tab.
home-empty-none-open: Shown in the New consultations tab when nothing is open to the reader. "Your consultations" is {{msg-proto|home-mode-yours}}, the other tab, which may still hold consultations they joined earlier.
home-output-dialog-close: Accessible label for the button closing the output-details dialog.
home-output-dialog-title: Default title of the dialog explaining why a consultation output is not ready yet.
common-return-home: Generic link back to the home page. Arrow is decorative in the template.
forbidden-elig-doc-title: Browser tab title of the not-eligible page. $1 is the consultation title, which is organizer-authored content and stays untranslated.
forbidden-elig-heading: Main heading when a user cannot join a consultation because they fail its eligibility check.
forbidden-elig-requirement: The eligibility rule on the not-eligible page, when the organizer has not named the requirement. When they have, {{msg-proto|forbidden-elig-requirement-named}} is used instead.
forbidden-elig-unavailable: Shown when the external eligibility checker service is down.
forbidden-elig-criteria: Shown when the user's account does not satisfy the eligibility rules.
forbidden-invite-doc-title: Browser tab title of every page that refuses entry to a consultation: not invited, no longer invited, not meeting its access conditions, or access that could not be confirmed. Site name included.
forbidden-invite-heading: Main heading when a consultation is restricted to invited participants.
forbidden-invite-body: Whole sentence telling the visitor they are not on the invite list. $1 is the consultation title, shown in bold; it is organizer-authored content and stays untranslated. Keep the <nowiki><strong></nowiki> tags.
forbidden-invite-mod-lead: Bold lead-in shown to moderators on the invite-only page.
forbidden-invite-mod-body: Tells a moderator how to also join as a participant; a link follows.
forbidden-invite-mod-link: Link to the invite-management admin page. Arrow is decorative.
forbidden-invite-back-home: Low-emphasis link back to the home page. Arrow is decorative.
forbidden-access-heading: Heading on the refusal page when a consultation limits who may take part and the check says no, for a reason other than a missing invitation (compare {{msg-proto|forbidden-invite-heading}}). The body is {{msg-proto|forbidden-access-body}}.
forbidden-access-body:
Body under {{msg-proto|forbidden-access-heading}}.

Parameters:
* $1 - the consultation's title, as its organizers wrote it.
forbidden-lost-heading: Heading on the refusal page for someone who joined this consultation earlier and no longer meets its access conditions. The body is {{msg-proto|forbidden-lost-body}}. When the access was an invitation, {{msg-proto|forbidden-lost-invite-heading}} is shown instead.
forbidden-lost-body:
Body under {{msg-proto|forbidden-lost-heading}}. It says only that new actions are stopped; what happens to earlier contributions is decided elsewhere, so the message makes no promise about them.

Parameters:
* $1 - the consultation's title, as its organizers wrote it.
forbidden-lost-invite-heading: Heading on the refusal page for someone who joined an invite-only consultation and has since been removed from its invite list. The body is {{msg-proto|forbidden-lost-invite-body}}.
forbidden-lost-invite-body:
Body under {{msg-proto|forbidden-lost-invite-heading}}. It says only that new actions are stopped; what happens to earlier contributions is decided elsewhere, so the message makes no promise about them.

Parameters:
* $1 - the consultation's title, as its organizers wrote it.
forbidden-unconfirmed-heading: Heading on the refusal page when the check of who may take part gave no answer, so the person is neither confirmed nor refused. The body is {{msg-proto|forbidden-unconfirmed-temporary}} or {{msg-proto|forbidden-unconfirmed-inconclusive}}.
forbidden-unconfirmed-temporary:
Body under {{msg-proto|forbidden-unconfirmed-heading}} when the check failed in a way expected to pass on a later try, such as a service that did not respond.

Parameters:
* $1 - the consultation's title, as its organizers wrote it.
forbidden-unconfirmed-inconclusive:
Body under {{msg-proto|forbidden-unconfirmed-heading}} when the check ran but could not reach a decision, so trying again will not change it.

guidance-statement-doc-title:
Browser tab/title for the statement-writing guide. Followed by the site name.
{{Identical|Writing good statements}}
guidance-statement-crumb: Header breadcrumb label for the statement-writing guide.
guidance-statement-heading:
Main heading of the statement-writing guide.
{{Identical|Writing good statements}}
guidance-statement-intro: Intro paragraph of the statement-writing guide. 'Agree', 'Disagree', 'Pass' are the vote options.
guidance-statement-check-one-claim: Checklist item (contains bold lead). Advises one claim per statement. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
guidance-statement-check-neutral: Checklist item (contains bold lead). Advises neutral wording. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
guidance-statement-check-specific: Checklist item (contains bold lead). Advises specificity. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
guidance-statement-check-statement: Checklist item (contains bold lead). Advises writing a statement, not a question. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
guidance-statement-split-label: Bold label introducing an example of splitting compound claims.
guidance-statement-split-body: Example showing how to split a compound statement into two.
guidance-statement-questions-label: Bold label introducing an example of turning a question into a claim.
guidance-statement-questions-body: Example showing how to rewrite a rhetorical question as a claim.
guidance-statement-pass-heading: Heading for the section explaining when to use the Pass vote.
guidance-statement-pass-body: Paragraph explaining when passing on a statement is appropriate.
guidance-argument-doc-title:
Browser tab/title for the argument-writing guide. Followed by the site name.
{{Identical|Writing good arguments}}
guidance-argument-crumb: Header breadcrumb label for the argument-writing guide.
guidance-argument-heading:
Main heading of the argument-writing guide.
{{Identical|Writing good arguments}}
guidance-argument-intro: Intro paragraph of the argument-writing guide.
guidance-argument-check-direction: Checklist item (bold lead). Advises stating for/against. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
guidance-argument-check-reason: Checklist item (bold lead). Advises giving a reason. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
guidance-argument-check-one-point: Checklist item (bold lead). Advises one point per argument. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
guidance-argument-check-specific: Checklist item (bold lead). Advises specificity. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
guidance-argument-check-claim: Checklist item (bold lead). Advises against personal attacks. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
guidance-argument-weak-label: Bold label for a weak example argument.
guidance-argument-strong-label: Bold label for a stronger example argument.
guidance-argument-moderation-body: Paragraph on moderation expectations for arguments.
output-eyebrow: Small label above an output's title on its page. $1 is the phase it is produced in, e.g. {{msg-proto|output-initial-clustering-phase}}. Rendered in capitals by CSS; write it in sentence case.
output-doc-title: Browser tab title of a consultation output's page. $1 is the output's name, e.g. {{msg-proto|output-report-label}} or {{msg-proto|output-argument-map-label}}; $2 is the consultation title, organizer-authored and untranslated. Proto is the product name.
output-status-pending: An output's status on its own page while it is not available yet. $1 is the status, {{msg-proto|output-status-provisional}} or {{msg-proto|output-status-final}}; "pending" describes the output. CSS capitalises the first letter of the line.
output-howto-heading: Heading for the explanatory box on an output detail page.
output-produced-from: Definition-list term: which phase produced this output.
output-method-label: Definition-list term: the method used to produce the output.
output-initial-clustering-heading: Section heading for the initial-clustering output.
output-initial-clustering-body: Placeholder description of the initial-clustering output.
output-initial-clustering-note: Italic note that the clustering visuals are not built yet.
output-argument-map-heading: Section heading for the argument-map output.
output-argument-map-body: Placeholder description of the argument-map output.
output-argument-map-link: Link to the Arguments tab of the live consultation. Arrow follows in the template.
output-preliminary-heading: Section heading for the preliminary-results output.
output-preliminary-body: Placeholder description of the preliminary-results output.
output-preliminary-link: Link to the preliminary-results tab of the live consultation. Arrow follows in the template.
output-dataset-heading: Section heading for the dataset output.
output-dataset-body: Placeholder description of the dataset output. 'xid' is an internal pseudonymous id; keep as-is.
output-dataset-note: Italic note that the dataset export is not built yet.
output-tbd-heading: Fallback section heading for an output type with no bespoke description yet.
reveal-crumb: Last part of the header breadcrumb on the identity-reveal page, where a participant may, after a consultation closes, permanently and publicly link their Wikimedia username to the pseudonym they used in it. Lowercase, like the other breadcrumb labels.
reveal-banner-identity: Small label above the heading of the identity-reveal page when the window is not open: before it opens, after it closed, or once the participant has linked their identity.
reveal-banner-window: Small label above the heading of the identity-reveal page while the participant can link their Wikimedia username, next to a globe icon. Rendered in capitals by CSS.
reveal-linked-heading: Heading of the identity-reveal page after the participant has linked their Wikimedia username to their pseudonym.
reveal-label-pseudonym:
Label above the participant's pseudonym on the identity card of the identity-reveal page. Rendered in capitals by CSS.
{{Identical|Pseudonym}}
reveal-label-username: Label above the participant's Wikimedia username on the identity card of the identity-reveal page. Rendered in capitals by CSS.
reveal-permanent-note: Note under the identity card once the participant has linked their identity: the platform will not remove the public link.
reveal-closed-heading: Heading of the identity-reveal page after linking has closed.
reveal-closed-body: Shown on the identity-reveal page after linking has closed: nobody can link their Wikimedia username to their pseudonym any more.
reveal-notyet-heading: Heading of the identity-reveal page before linking opens.
reveal-notyet-body: Shown on the identity-reveal page before linking opens. $1 is the date from which linking is possible, already formatted in the reader's language and shown in bold, e.g. "1 Oct 2026".
reveal-notyet-after: Second paragraph on the identity-reveal page before linking opens; follows {{msg-proto|reveal-notyet-body}}. Keep the <nowiki><strong></nowiki> tags.
reveal-open-heading: Heading of the identity-reveal page, where a participant may, after a consultation closes, permanently and publicly link their Wikimedia username to the pseudonym they used in it, while the window is open. $1 is the participant's pseudonym, e.g. "quiet-otter", shown in monospace; it is participant data and stays untranslated.
reveal-open-body:
Explanation under the heading of the identity-reveal page. Parameters:
* $1 - the participant's Wikimedia username, e.g. "ExampleUser"
* $2 - their pseudonym in this consultation, e.g. "quiet-otter"
Both are shown in monospace and stay untranslated. The participant's gender is unknown.
reveal-irreversible-label: Heading of the warning box on the identity-reveal page, listing the consequences of linking an identity. Describes the action.
reveal-irreversible-li1:
First point in the "Irreversible" warning on the identity-reveal page. Parameters:
* $1 - the participant's Wikimedia username, e.g. "ExampleUser", shown in bold
* $2 - their pseudonym, e.g. "quiet-otter", shown in bold
Both stay untranslated.
reveal-irreversible-li2: Second point in the "Irreversible" warning on the identity-reveal page.
reveal-irreversible-li3: Third point in the "Irreversible" warning on the identity-reveal page: internal records connecting username and pseudonym may be kept, separately from the public link.
reveal-consent:
Label of the required checkbox the participant ticks to confirm linking their identity. Parameters:
* $1 - their Wikimedia username, e.g. "ExampleUser", shown in bold
* $2 - their pseudonym, e.g. "quiet-otter", shown in bold
Both stay untranslated. The button that submits it is {{msg-proto|reveal-submit}}.
reveal-submit: Submit button on the identity-reveal page. The form cannot be submitted until {{msg-proto|reveal-consent}} is ticked. It links the participant's identity permanently.
reveal-submit-unavailable: Error under the button {{msg-proto|reveal-submit}} when the server refused the request because linking is not open (it closed, or has not opened yet). Nothing was linked. Shown to screen readers as an alert.
reveal-submit-unknown: Error under the button {{msg-proto|reveal-submit}} after any other failure, such as a lost connection. The request may still have succeeded, so this must not say the identity was not linked. Shown to screen readers as an alert.
reveal-tl-aria: Accessible label for the three-step identity-reveal timeline. The timeline appears on the identity-reveal page and in a closed consultation.
reveal-tl-closed-what: First step of the identity-reveal timeline: the consultation closed, and linking is not possible during the cooldown. $1 is the cooldown length in days, e.g. 30. The timeline appears on the identity-reveal page and in a closed consultation.
reveal-tl-step-inprogress: Screen-reader-only status for the waiting period after the consultation closed, while that step is current.
reveal-tl-step-completed:
Screen-reader-only status for a timeline step that is done.
{{Identical|(completed)}}
reveal-tl-opens-what: Second step of the identity-reveal timeline: linking opens. $1 is how many days linking stays possible, e.g. 30. The timeline appears on the identity-reveal page and in a closed consultation.
reveal-tl-step-current: Screen-reader-only status for the current timeline step.
reveal-tl-step-upcoming:
Screen-reader-only status for an upcoming timeline step.
{{Identical|(upcoming)}}
reveal-tl-closes-what: Third step of the identity-reveal timeline: linking closes, and after that nobody can link a Wikimedia username to a pseudonym. The timeline appears on the identity-reveal page and in a closed consultation.
reveal-tl-deadline-opens: Countdown line under the identity-reveal timeline while linking has not opened yet. $1 is the time left, {{msg-proto|reveal-tl-countdown}}, shown in bold. The timeline appears on the identity-reveal page and in a closed consultation.
reveal-tl-deadline-closes-permanent: Countdown line under the identity-reveal timeline while linking is open, so the warning that linking cannot be undone sits in the same sentence as the deadline. $1 is the time left, {{msg-proto|reveal-tl-countdown}}, shown in bold. The timeline appears on the identity-reveal page and in a closed consultation. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
reveal-tl-countdown:
Time left on the identity-reveal countdown, updated every second. It fills the $1 of {{msg-proto|reveal-tl-deadline-opens}} and {{msg-proto|reveal-tl-deadline-closes-permanent}}. Parameters:
* $1 - whole days left, e.g. 27; use {{PLURAL:$1|...}} if your language needs it
* $2 - hours, minutes and seconds left, e.g. "02:00:00"
The English "d" abbreviates days.
accept-crumb: Header breadcrumb label for the join/accept page.
accept-joining: Small label above the consultation title on the join page.
accept-reroll-aria: Accessible label for the reroll button.
accept-reroll: Reroll button text; the ↻ glyph regenerates pseudonym options.
accept-reroll-loading: Reroll button text while new options are loading.
accept-pseudonym-help: Helper text under the pseudonym-picker title.
accept-notify-help: Helper text for the notification-preference section. It covers both the email and the talk-page checkbox below it, and says that neither kind of notification is sent yet: the preference is stored for when the feature arrives.
accept-notify-email: Checkbox label opting into email notifications.
accept-notify-email-unavailable: Shown instead of the email-notification checkbox when the wiki account cannot be emailed. MediaWiki reports an account as emailable only when it has a confirmed address and accepts email from other users, so a missing address is one cause among several. $1 is a link to Wikimedia account preferences, labelled {{msg-proto|accept-notify-add-email}}, which opens in a new tab.
accept-notify-add-email: Link text inside {{msg-proto|accept-notify-email-unavailable}}, leading to Wikimedia account preferences on Meta-Wiki, where a confirmed address and email from other users are set.
accept-notify-talk: Checkbox label opting into talk-page notifications.
accept-privacy-details-summary: Summary/label of the expandable privacy details.
accept-privacy-body1: First paragraph of the expanded privacy details.
accept-privacy-body2: Second paragraph of the expanded privacy details.
accept-privacy-reveal-window:
The linking period, in the privacy details on the join screen. Parameters:
* $1 - the number of days after close when linking opens, e.g. 30
* $2 - the number of days after close when linking closes, e.g. 60
Keep the <nowiki><strong></nowiki> tags.
accept-licence-heading: Heading of the content-licence section on the join screen. Sits between the privacy summary and the consent checkbox.
accept-licence-intro: Licence disclosure on the join screen. $1 is a link to the CC0 deed, labelled with {{msg-proto|accept-licence-link}}, in parentheses after "public domain" to name the legal instrument. Do not translate the licence name itself.
accept-licence-link: Link label for the CC0 1.0 deed, used as $1 in {{msg-proto|accept-licence-intro}}. This is a licence name; keep it as-is.
accept-licence-scope: Second paragraph of the licence disclosure on the join screen, shown muted. Explains that the licence covers the text and not attribution, that the name shown is the pseudonym unless the participant links a Wikimedia username, that responses are excluded, and that the grant is irrevocable. This is an enforceable legal statement -- translate precisely and do not soften or omit any clause.
accept-consent: Label of the required consent checkbox on the join screen. This is the enforceable consent statement -- it must state all three clauses (CC0 release of what the participant writes, pseudonymous record, internal Wikimedia username link). Do not shorten.
accept-submit: Submit button on the join screen. $1 is the pseudonym the participant has selected, e.g. "quiet-otter"; it is participant data and stays untranslated, and updates as they pick another. The arrow is decorative.
accept-not-now: Low-emphasis link to leave without joining.
accept-js-selected: Screen-reader announcement after choosing a pseudonym; $1 is the name.
accept-js-regenerated: Screen-reader announcement after rerolling; $1 is the newly selected name.
reveal-callout-open-text: Callout shown while linking is open. $1 is the participant’s pseudonym, shown in bold, and is not translated. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
reveal-callout-link: Link in the reveal callout to the identity-linking page. Arrow follows in the template.
report-crumb: Header breadcrumb label for the final report page.
report-subtitle: Subtitle under the report title; a closed-date suffix may follow.
report-closed-suffix: Suffix before the consultation's close date in the report subtitle. Leading middle-dot.
report-badge-final: Badge marking the report as the final, frozen version.
report-status-final: Status value in the report's how-to-read box.
report-intro-heading: Section heading for the report introduction.
report-intro-placeholder: Italic placeholder where the organizer introduction will go.
report-process-heading: Section heading for the consultation process timeline.
report-process-opened: Timeline label: when the consultation opened.
report-process-submission: Timeline label for the Explore phase, the first round, where participants respond to statements and add their own. Uses the same name as {{msg-proto|phase-label-submission}}.
report-process-dates-tbd: Placeholder where a phase's dates are not recorded yet.
report-process-argmap: Timeline label for the Arguments phase, when participants write arguments for and against featured statements. Uses the same name as {{msg-proto|phase-label-argument_mapping}}.
report-process-informed:
Timeline label for the informed opinion phase. Uses the same name as {{msg-proto|phase-label-informed_voting}}.
{{Identical|Informed opinion}}
report-process-closed: Timeline label: when the consultation closed.
report-participation-p2: Stat label under a participant count: people who took part in the Explore round, the first round of responses.
report-participation-p6: Stat label under a participant count: people who took part in the informed opinion round.
report-participation-both: Stat label under a participant count: people who took part in both rounds. The value is a placeholder for now.
report-moderation-applied: Lead-in before counts of moderation exclusions.
report-moderation-stmts: Count of statements excluded by moderation. $1 is the number.
report-moderation-parts: Count of participants excluded by moderation. Leading middle-dot separator; $1 is the number.
report-participation-unavailable: Shown when the results database cannot be reached.
report-statements-heading:
Section heading for the statement inventory.
{{Identical|Statements}}
report-statements-placeholder: Italic placeholder for the statement inventory.
report-featured-count: Count of featured statements. $1 is the number.
report-initial-heading: Section heading for the opinions from the Explore round, the first round of responses.
report-bar-title:
Tooltip on a vote bar in the final report. Parameters:
* $1 - the agree percentage, already formatted for your language with its percent sign, e.g. "62.5%"
* $2 - the disagree percentage, formatted the same way
* $3 - the pass percentage, formatted the same way
Do not add a percent sign; it comes with the number.
report-bar-label:
Label under a bar in the final report showing how a statement was answered. Parameters:
* $1 - the agree percentage, already formatted for your language with its percent sign, e.g. "62.5%"
* $2 - the pass percentage, formatted the same way
* $3 - the number of responses (one per participant)
Do not add a percent sign; it comes with the number.
report-most-divisive: Sub-heading listing the most divisive statements.
report-argmap-heading:
Section heading for the argument-mapping summary.
{{Identical|Argument mapping}}
report-argmap-placeholder: Italic placeholder for the argument-mapping summary.
report-shift-heading: Section heading for the aggregate opinion-shift analysis.
report-shift-intro: Intro paragraph above the opinion-shift table. $1 is a link to the Methodology section of the same report, labelled with {{msg-proto|report-methodology-link}} — e.g. Methodology. The parenthetical used to be three separate messages, which fixed the English word order; it is one sentence now, so move "$1" and "below" wherever your language needs them. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
report-methodology-link:
Link text pointing to the Methodology section.
{{Identical|Methodology}}
report-shift-sorted: Note that the opinion-shift table is sorted by shift magnitude.
report-col-statement:
Table column header: the statement text.
{{Identical|Statement}}
report-col-initial: Table column header: the responses from the Explore round, the first round. Uses the same name as {{msg-proto|phase-label-submission}}.
report-col-informed:
Table column header: the informed opinion round (Phase 6).
{{Identical|Informed opinion}}
report-col-shift:
Table column header: the opinion shift.
{{Identical|Shift}}
report-col-shift-note: Small note under the Shift column header clarifying it is an aggregate.
report-table-aria: Accessible label for the opinion-shift table.
report-matched-heading: Section heading for the analysis of participants who responded in both the Explore round and the informed opinion round.
report-matched-placeholder: Italic placeholder for the matched-participant analysis.
report-matched-note: Caveat about the change measured for participants present in both rounds, and about extending it to everyone.
report-groups-heading: Section heading for the opinion-group clusters.
report-groups-sub: Sub-label with the number of opinion groups. $1 is the count.
report-group-label: Heading of one opinion group, in the intermediate results and in the final report. $1 is the group's number, starting at 1.
report-group-members: Member count for an opinion group. Leading middle-dot; $1 is the number.
report-badge-agree:
Badge marking a statement the group agreed with.
{{Identical|agree}}
report-badge-disagree:
Badge marking a statement the group disagreed with.
{{Identical|disagree}}
report-landed-heading: Heading of the personalised self-comparison section.
report-landed-body: Placeholder body for the personalised self-comparison.
report-methodology-heading:
Section heading for the methodology explanation.
{{Identical|Methodology}}
report-methodology-sources-body: Data-sources methodology paragraph (contains an inline code span for a DB view name). Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
report-methodology-shift-body: Methodology paragraph for the aggregate shift (contains inline em and bold). Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
report-methodology-delta-body: Methodology paragraph for individual delta and extrapolation.
report-methodology-delta-placeholder: Italic placeholder for the CI methodology.
report-methodology-clustering-body: Methodology paragraph for the clustering algorithm.
report-no-results: Shown when the informed opinion round has produced no results to report.
conv-crumb-aria: Accessible label for the header breadcrumb on a consultation page.
conv-crumb-about: Header breadcrumb link from the conversation workspace to the consultation’s about page.
about-doc-title: Browser tab title of a consultation's About page. $1 is the consultation title, organizer-authored and untranslated. Proto is the product name.
about-eyebrow: Small label above the heading of a consultation's About page, which summarises its state, statistics and outputs. Rendered in capitals by CSS; write it in sentence case.
about-heading: Heading of a consultation's About page. $1 is the consultation title, organizer-authored and untranslated.
about-status-heading: Section heading on the About page for the consultation's current status, phase and next scheduled change.
about-status-label: Bold label on the About page; {{msg-proto|about-status-open}}, {{msg-proto|about-status-paused}} or {{msg-proto|about-status-closed}} follows.
about-status-open:
Consultation status on the About page: participants can take part. Describes the consultation.
{{Identical|Open}}
about-status-paused:
Consultation status on the About page: an organizer has paused it. Describes the consultation.
{{Identical|Paused}}
about-status-closed:
Consultation status on the About page: it has ended. Describes the consultation.
{{Identical|Closed}}
about-phase-label: Bold label on the About page; the names of the active phases follow, e.g. {{msg-proto|phase-label-submission}}. $1 is how many phases are active, usually 1.
about-pseudonym-label: Bold label on the About page; the participant's pseudonym in this consultation follows.
about-stats-heading: Section heading on the About page for the consultation's totals.
about-stat-participants: Unit under a large number on the About page. $1 is that number, used only to choose the plural form; it is shown separately above. When the value is unknown a dash is shown instead of the number, and $1 is 100, so use the form a general plural takes.
about-stat-statement-votes: Unit under a large number on the About page: responses given to statements. $1 is that number, used only to choose the plural form. When the value is unknown a dash is shown instead of the number, and $1 is 100, so use the form a general plural takes.
about-stat-statements: Unit under a large number on the About page. $1 is that number, used only to choose the plural form. When the value is unknown a dash is shown instead of the number, and $1 is 100, so use the form a general plural takes.
about-stat-arguments: Unit under a large number on the About page. $1 is that number, used only to choose the plural form. When the value is unknown a dash is shown instead of the number, and $1 is 100, so use the form a general plural takes.
about-stat-argument-contributors: Unit under a large number on the About page: participants who wrote at least one argument. $1 is that number, used only to choose the plural form. When the value is unknown a dash is shown instead of the number, and $1 is 100, so use the form a general plural takes.
about-stat-unknown: Screen-reader text for a statistic on the About page whose value could not be loaded; sighted readers see a dash in its place. Describes the number.
about-stats-unavailable: Note on the About page when the participant and response totals cannot be loaded from the voting service (Polis); argument totals still show. Polis is the name of the software and is not translated.
about-contrib-heading: Section heading on the About page listing what the participant has contributed to this consultation.
about-contrib-suggested: List item on the About page. $1 is the number of statements the participant proposed.
about-contrib-votes: List item on the About page. $1 is the number of statements the participant has responded to.
about-contrib-votes-unavailable: List item on the About page when the participant's response count cannot be loaded.
about-contrib-arguments-added: List item on the About page. $1 is the number of arguments the participant wrote.
about-contrib-arguments-rated: List item on the About page. $1 is the number of arguments the participant marked as most important.
about-outputs-heading: Section heading on the About page listing the consultation's outputs, such as {{msg-proto|output-report-label}}.
about-output-pending: An output that is not available yet, in the list on the About page. $1 is the output's name, e.g. {{msg-proto|output-report-label}}; the rest of the line is shown muted. "Pending" describes the output.
about-modlog-link-count: Link on the About page to the consultation's public moderation log. $1 is the number of recorded events. With no events, {{msg-proto|conv-moderation-log}} is used.
about-return: Link on the About page back to the consultation itself.
conv-crumb-manage: Header link for moderators to open the admin view of this consultation.
conv-flag-aria-statement: Accessible label of the flag icon on a statement (Explore tab and Arguments tab); it opens a short form to report the statement to moderators.
conv-flag-aria-argument: Accessible label of the flag icon on a participant's argument in the Arguments tab; it opens a short form to report the argument to moderators.
conv-flag-reason-label:
Visually hidden label of the reason dropdown in the flag form.
{{Identical|Reason}}
conv-flag-cat-personal: Reason in the flag form's dropdown: a personal attack.
conv-flag-cat-privacy: Reason in the flag form's dropdown: a privacy violation.
conv-flag-cat-offtopic: Reason in the flag form's dropdown: off-topic content.
conv-flag-cat-other: Reason in the flag form's dropdown: some other reason; details are then required.
conv-flag-details-label:
Visually hidden label of the details box in the flag form.
{{Identical|Details}}
conv-flag-details-placeholder: Placeholder in the details box of the flag form, for any reason other than {{msg-proto|conv-flag-cat-other}}.
conv-flag-send:
Submit button of the flag form that reports a statement or argument to moderators.
{{Identical|Send}}
conv-flag-details-required-placeholder: Placeholder in the details box of the flag form when the reason is {{msg-proto|conv-flag-cat-other}}; details are then required. Otherwise {{msg-proto|conv-flag-details-placeholder}} is shown.
conv-flag-thanks: Confirmation shown in the flag form after a report is sent. It closes on its own after a couple of seconds.
conv-demo-label:
Bold label marking a demo consultation.
{{Identical|Demo}}
conv-space-warn-live-label: Bold lead-in of the banner shown when a participant lands on a REAL consultation they did not explicitly choose. Must read as a warning that this is the genuine thing, never as a demo. Pairs with conv-space-warn-live-body.
conv-space-warn-live-body: Body of the real-consultation banner: tells the participant their responses are counted, then invites anyone only exploring to leave for the demo. Keep as one sentence pair; a translation must not suggest the responses are practice ones. Followed by {{msg-proto|conv-space-warn-live-link}}.
conv-space-warn-live-link: Link at the end of the real-consultation banner, offering the demo space to someone who only wanted to look around.
conv-space-warn-demo-label: Bold lead-in of the banner shown when a participant lands on a DEMONSTRATION consultation. Must read as "not real", never as a live consultation. Pairs with conv-space-warn-demo-body.
conv-space-warn-demo-body: Body of the demo banner: tells the participant this is not a real consultation. Keep as one sentence; a translation must not let it be read as a live consultation. Followed by {{msg-proto|conv-space-warn-demo-link}}.
conv-space-warn-demo-link: Link at the end of the demo banner, leading to the index of demonstration consultations.
conv-space-warn-ok: Button that dismisses the real/demo banner for this visit. Acknowledgement, not consent.
conv-demo-mode-lock: Persistent notice at the top of every demonstration consultation, unlike the dismissible banner. Says the mechanics behave normally while the consultation itself is not real; a translation must keep both halves.
conv-scheduled-transition: Notice about a consultation's next phase change, when one is scheduled: above the consultation, and on its About page. $1 is the name of the phase it moves to, shown in bold; $2 is the date and time, already formatted in the reader’s own timezone. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
conv-scheduled-tz-title: Tooltip on the date of the next scheduled phase change, telling the reader the time is converted to their own timezone.
conv-closed-on: Opening paragraph on a closed consultation: says when it closed and that responses were recorded pseudonymously, with a limited period in which a Wikimedia username can be linked. $1 is the close date, shown in bold. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
conv-revealed-text: Shown to a participant who has already linked their identity. $1 is their pseudonym, shown in bold, and is not translated. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
conv-reveal-pending-opens: Shown before the linking period opens. $1 is the date it opens.
conv-reveal-expired: Shown once the linking period has ended.
conv-closed-simple: Simple closed-state message when no reveal context applies.
conv-read-report: Link to the final report: on the screen shown once someone has given their informed opinion, after {{msg-proto|conv-p6-done-closed}}, and on its own in a closed consultation. A decorative arrow follows.
conv-paused: Shown when a consultation is paused.
conv-nothing-available: Shown when no participation tab is available yet.
conv-tab-vote:
Tab label for the tab where participants respond to short statements and add their own. Named after the phase, {{msg-proto|phase-label-submission}}.
{{Identical|Explore}}
conv-tab-results: Tab label for the intermediate results.
conv-tab-arguments:
Tab label for the argument-mapping phase.
{{Identical|Arguments}}
conv-tab-informed:
Tab label for the informed opinion round.
{{Identical|Informed opinion}}
conv-tab-preliminary:
Tab label (and section label) for the preliminary results of the informed opinion round.
{{Identical|Preliminary results}}
conv-vote-voted-label: Label after the 'done / total' count in the progress row, e.g. "12 / 30 responses".
conv-vote-progress-aria: Accessible label for the response progress bar.
conv-vote-progress-valuetext: Spoken value of the response progress bar. $1 is how many statements the participant has responded to, $2 the total.
conv-vote-statement-label:
Small caps label above the current statement card. Rendered in capitals by CSS; write it in sentence case.
{{Identical|Statement}}
conv-vote-private: Small label on the statement card noting that the participant's response is private.
conv-vote-you-voted: Confirmation badge after responding to a statement. $1 is the option the participant chose, supplied by {{msg-proto|conv-vote-agree}}, {{msg-proto|conv-vote-disagree}} or {{msg-proto|conv-vote-pass}} — e.g. "Agree". Rendered in capitals by CSS, so write it in sentence case.
conv-vote-change: Button to change a just-cast vote.
conv-loading: Placeholder while the consultation workspace is still being fetched.
conv-unavailable-doc-title: Browser tab title when the consultation workspace could not be loaded.
conv-unavailable-heading: Heading of the error screen shown when the consultation workspace could not be loaded. The reason from the server is printed below it.
conv-doc-title: Browser tab title for the conversation workspace. $1 is the consultation title, which is participant-facing content and stays untranslated.
conv-vote-agree:
Vote label: agree. The label of the response button in the Explore tab and on informed opinion cards, and $1 of {{msg-proto|conv-vote-you-voted}}. The confirmation in the informed opinion round and the Yours column use the past tense, {{msg-proto|conv-p6-voted-agree}}.
{{Identical|Agree}}
conv-vote-pass: Vote label: pass. The label of the response button in the Explore tab and on informed opinion cards, and $1 of {{msg-proto|conv-vote-you-voted}}. The confirmation in the informed opinion round and the Yours column use the past tense, {{msg-proto|conv-p6-voted-pass}}. Pass means the participant chose neither agree nor disagree; it does not mean approved.
conv-vote-disagree:
Vote label: disagree. The label of the response button in the Explore tab and on informed opinion cards, and $1 of {{msg-proto|conv-vote-you-voted}}. The confirmation in the informed opinion round and the Yours column use the past tense, {{msg-proto|conv-p6-voted-disagree}}.
{{Identical|Disagree}}
conv-triad-idle-label: Label above the post-vote option triad, shown before the participant has responded.
conv-triad-active-label: Label above the option triad, shown after voting.
conv-triad-alldone-label: Label above the option triad when all statements are done.
conv-triad-suggest-title: Triad option / composer title: suggest a reworded version of the statement.
conv-triad-suggest-sub: Sub-text of the 'suggest wording' triad option.
conv-triad-suggest-action: Action text of the 'suggest wording' triad option. Arrow decorative.
conv-triad-next-title: Triad option: move to the next statement.
conv-triad-next-sub: Sub-text of the 'move on' triad option.
conv-triad-next-action:
Action text of the 'move on' triad option. Arrow decorative.
{{Identical|Next →}}
conv-triad-newstmt-title: Triad option / composer title: propose a brand-new statement.
conv-triad-newstmt-action: Action text of the 'propose new statement' option. Arrow decorative.
conv-suggest-helper: Helper text in the suggest-wording composer; a 'Writing tips' link follows.
conv-suggest-placeholder: Example placeholder in the suggest-wording textarea.
conv-suggest-hint: Note under the box for suggesting clearer wording of an existing statement, saying where the suggestion goes and that the wording is released under CC0, as agreed on joining ({{msg-proto|accept-licence-intro}}). "CC0" is the licence name and is not translated.
conv-composer-submit: Submit button in the statement composers.
conv-composer-charcount: Character counter under the statement composer. $1 is the number of characters typed so far; 280 is the fixed limit.
conv-newstmt-helper: Helper text in the new-statement composer; a 'Writing tips' link follows.
conv-newstmt-hint: Note under the box for writing a new statement, saying that others respond to it too and that it is released under CC0, as agreed on joining ({{msg-proto|accept-licence-intro}}). "CC0" is the licence name and is not translated.
conv-proposed: Confirmation badge after proposing a statement.
conv-propose-next:
Button to move to the next statement after proposing. Arrow follows.
{{Identical|Next statement}}
conv-alldone-label: Shown when the participant has responded to every statement available to them in the conversation.
conv-alldone-sub: Sub-text encouraging proposing statements when all are done.
conv-error-load: Error shown when statements fail to load.
conv-results-heading: Heading of the intermediate results tab; a participant count may follow.
conv-participant-count: How many people took part, shown in small muted text after {{msg-proto|conv-results-heading}} on the intermediate results tab, and in the header of the preliminary results. $1 is the number of participants, e.g. 24; the count is not shown when it is 0. Starts lowercase in English, as it continues the heading line.
conv-small-sample: Warning above the intermediate results when few people have voted. $1 is the number of participants, e.g. 12. Keep the <nowiki><strong></nowiki> tags.
conv-results-quoted: A participant's statement quoted in the results, in the intermediate results tab and the final report. $1 is the statement, e.g. "Shared maintenance matters."; use your language's quotation marks.
conv-consensus-label: Label above the list of statements that most participants agreed or disagreed with, on the intermediate results tab. Rendered in capitals by CSS; write it in sentence case.
conv-badge-agree:
Lowercase badge before a statement in the intermediate results: overall or within one opinion group, most participants agreed with it.
{{Identical|agree}}
conv-badge-disagree:
Lowercase badge before a statement in the intermediate results: overall or within one opinion group, most participants disagreed with it.
{{Identical|disagree}}
conv-groups-found: Label above the opinion groups on the intermediate results tab. $1 is the number of opinion groups found, e.g. 2 or 3; each group follows under its own {{msg-proto|report-group-label}}. Rendered in capitals by CSS; write it in sentence case.
conv-results-pending: Shown before enough votes exist for results.
conv-results-unpublished: Shown when results are not published.
conv-arg-none: Shown when no featured statements exist for argument mapping.
conv-orient-full:
Orientation banner at the top of the Arguments tab, first paragraph, followed by {{msg-proto|conv-orient-then}}. Keep the and tags; no other markup is allowed, and a
in particular makes the whole message unreadable.
conv-orient-then: Second paragraph of the orientation banner on the Arguments tab, under {{msg-proto|conv-orient-full}}: what happens once both sides are handled.
conv-orient-mini: Collapsed form of the orientation banner in the Arguments tab. Keep the <nowiki><strong></nowiki> tags; no other markup is allowed.
conv-orient-collapse: Toggle text to collapse the orientation banner. A ▲ glyph follows. Lowercase on purpose: it is a small inline control.
conv-orient-whatis: Toggle text to expand the collapsed orientation banner. A ▼ glyph follows. Lowercase on purpose: it is a small inline control.
conv-arg-complete-title: Heading shown when every argument panel is complete.
conv-arg-complete-sub: Sub-text shown when the participant has been through every featured statement. Marking the most important arguments stays open only on statements that have enough arguments.
conv-arg-featured-label: Label above a featured statement in the arguments tab.
conv-arg-panel-expand-aria: Accessible label of a finished featured-statement panel's header while collapsed; activating it shows the arguments again.
conv-arg-panel-collapse-aria: Accessible label of a finished featured-statement panel's header while expanded; activating it hides the arguments.
conv-arg-step1-name: Name of step 1 of the two-step task in the Arguments tab. Keep the digit and the separator.
conv-arg-step1-sub-none: Progress line under "1 · Add arguments" on a featured statement in the Arguments tab. "for" and "against" are the two sides (arguments supporting or opposing the statement); a ✓ marks a side the participant has handled by adding an argument or choosing to add nothing. Keep the marks and the separator. Neither side handled yet.
conv-arg-step1-sub-for: Progress line under "1 · Add arguments" on a featured statement in the Arguments tab. "for" and "against" are the two sides (arguments supporting or opposing the statement); a ✓ marks a side the participant has handled by adding an argument or choosing to add nothing. Keep the marks and the separator. The for side is handled.
conv-arg-step1-sub-against: Progress line under "1 · Add arguments" on a featured statement in the Arguments tab. "for" and "against" are the two sides (arguments supporting or opposing the statement); a ✓ marks a side the participant has handled by adding an argument or choosing to add nothing. Keep the marks and the separator. The against side is handled.
conv-arg-step1-sub-both: Progress line under "1 · Add arguments" on a featured statement in the Arguments tab. "for" and "against" are the two sides (arguments supporting or opposing the statement); a ✓ marks a side the participant has handled by adding an argument or choosing to add nothing. Keep the marks and the separator. Both sides are handled.
conv-arg-step2-name: Name of step 2 of the two-step task in the Arguments tab. Keep the digit and the separator.
conv-arg-step2-sub:
Progress line under "2 · Prioritise" once step 1 is done. Parameters:
* $1 - for-arguments the participant marked, e.g. 1
* $2 - how many for-arguments they may mark, e.g. 2
* $3 - against-arguments marked, e.g. 0
* $4 - how many against-arguments they may mark, e.g. 1
conv-arg-step2-locked: Step-2 sub-line while step 2 is still locked.
conv-arg-col-for: Header for supporting (for) arguments: a column in the Arguments tab, and a side of each informed opinion card. Rendered in capitals by CSS; write it in sentence case. See also {{msg-proto|conv-arg-col-against}}.
conv-arg-col-against: Header for opposing (against) arguments: a column in the Arguments tab, and a side of each informed opinion card. Rendered in capitals by CSS; write it in sentence case. See also {{msg-proto|conv-arg-col-for}}.
conv-arg-add-for: Button on the for side of a featured statement; it opens a box for writing one argument supporting the statement. Each participant adds at most one argument per side. See also {{msg-proto|conv-arg-add-against}}.
conv-arg-add-against: Button on the against side of a featured statement; it opens a box for writing one argument opposing the statement. Each participant adds at most one argument per side. See also {{msg-proto|conv-arg-add-for}}.
conv-arg-nothing:
Button on one side of a featured statement: the participant has no argument to add on that side. The resulting state is {{msg-proto|conv-arg-skipped}}.
{{Identical|Nothing to add}}
conv-arg-composer-label-for: Label above the box for writing one argument supporting the statement. Keep the middle dot. See also {{msg-proto|conv-arg-composer-label-against}}.
conv-arg-composer-label-against: Label above the box for writing one argument opposing the statement. Keep the middle dot. See also {{msg-proto|conv-arg-composer-label-for}}.
conv-arg-placeholder-for:
Placeholder in the box for writing one argument supporting the statement. See also {{msg-proto|conv-arg-placeholder-against}}. Parameters:
* $1 - the most characters an argument may have, e.g. 280
conv-arg-placeholder-against:
Placeholder in the box for writing one argument opposing the statement. See also {{msg-proto|conv-arg-placeholder-for}}. Parameters:
* $1 - the most characters an argument may have, e.g. 280
conv-arg-submit: Submit button in the argument composer.
conv-arg-added-for: Shown on the for side once the participant has added their argument there. See also {{msg-proto|conv-arg-added-against}}.
conv-arg-added-against: Shown on the against side once the participant has added their argument there. See also {{msg-proto|conv-arg-added-for}}.
conv-arg-changemind: Link-styled button after {{msg-proto|conv-arg-skipped}} that reopens the argument box. Lowercase on purpose.
conv-arg-skipped:
Status shown on one side of a featured statement after the participant chose to add no argument there. Followed by {{msg-proto|conv-arg-changemind}}. The button that makes this choice is {{msg-proto|conv-arg-nothing}}; this is the resulting state.
{{Identical|Nothing to add}}
conv-arg-save-error: Error under the argument composer when submitting an argument, or choosing to add nothing, fails.
conv-arg-locked-note: Note on one side of a featured statement (in favour or against) while the participant has neither added an argument there nor chosen {{msg-proto|conv-arg-nothing}}, and that side has no arguments yet. Nothing is hidden from them: other participants' arguments appear as soon as they exist, whatever the participant has done. Marking the most important arguments opens once both sides are handled and a side holds more arguments than the participant may mark.
conv-arg-mark: Accessible name of the toggle on an argument that marks it as one of the most important. Its pressed state tells assistive technology whether it is marked, so the name stays the same either way.

adminconv-label-polis-id: Label of a read-only fact in the admin console: the identifier of the Polis conversation behind this consultation. "zinvite" is Polis’ own name for it and is not translated.
adminconv-label-tier: Label for the complexity tier, which sets the recommended quantities. Shown as a read-only fact in the admin console; the tier itself is chosen on the settings page.
adminconv-danger-label: Section label for the danger zone.
adminconv-perm-closed: Danger-row title when the consultation is closed.
adminconv-view-report: Link to the final report. Arrow follows.
adminconv-reveal-ended: Shown when the linking period has ended.
adminconv-closed-cannot-reopen: Shown after a close date when there is no reveal context.
adminconv-publish-report: Title/button to publish the final report.
adminconv-publish-unavailable: Shown when publishing the report is not yet available.
adminconv-cleanup-li4: Cleanup checklist: wrote the report intro.
adminconv-delete-title: Danger-row title: delete an empty consultation.
adminconv-delete-hasvotes: Deletion disabled because responses exist. $1 is the number of responses.
adminconv-confirm-publish: Confirm dialog before publishing the final report.
adminconv-confirm-delete: Confirm dialog before deleting the consultation.
adminconv-due-now: JS countdown text once a scheduled transition is due.
flash-import-rejected-rows: Import rejected: too many rows. $1 source label, $2 line count, $3 max. Keep the leading ✗.
flash-import-row-error: A single import row error. $1 is the row number, $2 the reason (data).
flash-import-rejected-invalid: Import rejected because a line was invalid. Keep the leading ✗.
flash-skipped: A skipped import line. $1 is the reason (data).
flash-import-no-valid-rows: Import produced nothing because no rows were valid.
flash-import-no-result: Import where Polis returned nothing. Keep the leading ⚠.
flash-flag-resolved: Confirmation that a moderation flag was resolved.
flash-phases-saved-sync-failed: Warning: phases saved but Polis sync failed.
flash-custom-phase-state: Error: phases in a custom state.
flash-move-sync-failed: Warning: phase moved but Polis sync failed.
flash-moved-to: Confirmation naming the new phase. $1 is the phase label (data).
flash-last-featured-hide: Error: cannot hide the last featured statement during argument mapping.
flash-seed-added-no-link: Warning: seed added but correction link failed.
flash-seed-added-corrected: Confirmation: seed added as a correction. $1 is the corrected statement id.
flash-last-featured-remove: Error: cannot remove the last featured statement during argument mapping.

adminconv-command-failed: Fallback toast when an admin console action fails and the server sent no explanation of its own.
adminconv-countdown-days: Compact day unit in the countdown to a scheduled phase transition, e.g. "2d 4h 30m". $1 is the number of days. Keep it to a letter or two.
adminconv-countdown-hours: Compact hour unit in the countdown to a scheduled phase transition. $1 is the number of hours. Keep it to a letter or two.
adminconv-countdown-minutes: Compact minute unit in the countdown to a scheduled phase transition. $1 is the number of minutes. Keep it to a letter or two.
adminconv-countdown-lt1m: Countdown shown when a scheduled transition is under a minute away but not yet due; the other units are {{msg-proto|adminconv-countdown-minutes}} and its siblings. Keep it very short, in words, e.g. "under 1 min". Do not use <nowiki><</nowiki>: the message cannot be parsed with it. Do not use an HTML entity either: the countdown is plain text, so it would show literally.
adminconv-status-published: Pill beside the report phase name: the final report has been published.
adminconv-status-unpublished: Pill beside the report phase name: the report phase is reached but the report has not been published.
adminconv-phase-desc-published: Description under the current-phase name once the report is published, replacing the phase effect text.
adminconv-report-published-note: Note in place of the move-on box when there is nothing left to advance to and the report is published. The <nowiki><strong></nowiki> emphasis is part of the sentence.
adminconv-report-unpublished-note: Note in place of the move-on box when the report phase is reached but not published; points the organizer at the publish control lower down. The <nowiki><strong></nowiki> emphasis is part of the sentence.
adminconv-roles-summary-count: Disclosure summary for the roles list when roles are assigned. $1 is how many.
adminconv-assigned-count: Count badge on the "Roles" card of the admin console. $1 is the number of role assignments in this consultation, e.g. 4.
adminconv-publish-irrev: Warning under the publish-report control once the cleanup period is open. $1 is the report URL path; the <nowiki><code></nowiki> markup around it is part of the message.
adminconv-closed-on: Opens the danger-zone description of a closed consultation. $1 is the close date. A sentence about the identity-reveal window follows.
adminconv-closed-undated: Used instead of adminconv-closed-on when no close date was recorded.
adminconv-reveal-pending: Danger-zone description before the linking period opens. $1 is the opening date, $2 the number of days until then.
adminconv-reveal-open-date: Danger-zone description while participants can still link their Wikimedia username. $1 is the closing date.
base-mode-switch-aria: Accessible name for the demo/real toggle in the site header. Names the choice, since the two options alone do not say what is being switched.
base-mode-demo: The demo option in the header's demo/real toggle. A call to action, not a noun — it invites the visitor into a practice consultation. Sits beside {{msg-proto|base-mode-real}}.
base-mode-real: The real-consultation option in the header's demo/real toggle, beside {{msg-proto|base-mode-demo}}. Short because it is one half of a two-option switch.
base-lock-real: Badge in the header of a real consultation, marking that what the participant does here counts. The demo counterpart is {{msg-proto|conv-demo-label}}.
base-footer-licence: Licence line in the site footer. $1 is a link to the CC0 deed labelled with {{msg-proto|accept-licence-link}} — e.g. CC0. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
fork-demo-title: Heading of the card leading to a demonstration consultation.
fork-demo-sub: Subtitle under {{msg-proto|fork-demo-title}}: what the demo card offers.
fork-demo-cta: Call to action on the demo card. The arrow is decorative.
fork-demo-aria: Accessible name for the whole demo card, which is one link. Says both the heading and the subtitle, since a screen-reader user hears the link name in place of the card.
fork-real-title: Heading of the card leading to live consultations.
fork-real-sub: Subtitle under {{msg-proto|fork-real-title}}: the point of difference from the demo card.
fork-real-cta: Call to action on the real-consultations card. The arrow is decorative.
fork-real-aria: Accessible name for the whole real-consultations card, which is one link.
base-language-label: Accessible name for the language switcher in the site header. The options are language autonyms and are never translated — a reader looking for Dutch scans for "Nederlands".
base-loading-conversations: Shown while the app is still fetching. It renders before the message catalogue has loaded, so the server stamps it into the page; see {{msg-proto|base-skip-to-content}}, which is delivered the same way.
errorpage-code: Small label above the heading on a server error page. $1 is the HTTP status code, e.g. 404.
errorpage-404-hint: What to do next, on the 404 page. Keep the HTML and the text inside it — it links to the front page.
errorpage-403-title: Heading of the 403 page. An adjective describing the request, not the person.
errorpage-403-hint: What to do next, on the 403 page.
errorpage-500-hint: What to do next, on the 500 page.
accept-js-taken: Live-region announcement when the chosen pseudonym was claimed by someone else between the page loading and the form being submitted. Fresh options are offered.
forbidden-elig-requirement-named: The eligibility rule on the not-eligible page, when the organizer named one. $1 is that name, shown in bold — organizer-authored content, so it stays untranslated. When no name is configured, {{msg-proto|forbidden-elig-requirement}} is used instead. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
forbidden-voucher-heading: Heading on the refusal page of a consultation that admits only people with a voucher (a one-time access code handed out by its organizers), shown to someone who is not signed in with one. The body is {{msg-proto|forbidden-voucher-body}}, followed by the link {{msg-proto|forbidden-voucher-link}}.
forbidden-voucher-body:
Body under {{msg-proto|forbidden-voucher-heading}}.

Parameters:
* $1 - the consultation's title, as its organizers wrote it.
forbidden-voucher-link: Link under {{msg-proto|forbidden-voucher-body}}, to the page where a voucher code is typed in (its heading is the consultation title, its field label {{msg-proto|voucher-page-label}}).
forbidden-voucher-other-heading: Heading on the refusal page when someone signed in with a voucher account opens a different consultation. A voucher account exists for one consultation only. The body is {{msg-proto|forbidden-voucher-other-body}}.
forbidden-voucher-other-body:
Body under {{msg-proto|forbidden-voucher-other-heading}}.

Parameters:
* $1 - the title of the consultation that was opened, as its organizers wrote it.
forbidden-lost-voucher-heading: Heading on the refusal page for someone who joined with a voucher that the organizers have since revoked. Compare {{msg-proto|forbidden-lost-heading}}. The body is {{msg-proto|forbidden-lost-voucher-body}}.
forbidden-lost-voucher-body:
Body under {{msg-proto|forbidden-lost-voucher-heading}}. It says only that new actions are stopped; what happens to earlier contributions is decided elsewhere, so the message makes no promise about them.

Parameters:
* $1 - the consultation's title, as its organizers wrote it.
base-voucher-account: Shown in the page header, where a Wikimedia username appears for other people, when the visitor is signed in with a voucher account (an account created from a one-time access code, which has no username). Lower case to match {{msg-proto|base-log-out}} beside it.
voucher-page-doc-title:
Browser tab title of the page where a voucher code (a one-time access code handed out by a consultation's organizers) is typed in.

Parameters:
* $1 - the consultation's title, as its organizers wrote it.
voucher-page-intro: Sentence under the consultation title on the voucher code page, above the field {{msg-proto|voucher-page-label}}.
voucher-page-label: Label of the text field on the voucher code page.
voucher-page-hint: Help text under the voucher code field ({{msg-proto|voucher-page-label}}). Codes are compared ignoring upper/lower case, spaces and hyphens, so people may type them with spaces or hyphens between groups.
voucher-page-submit: Button that submits the voucher code.
voucher-error-empty: Error under the voucher code field when the form is submitted empty.
voucher-error-too-short:
Error under the voucher code field when what was typed is shorter than any voucher code can be (spaces and hyphens are not counted). The typed text stays in the field so it can be completed.

Parameters:
* $1 - the minimum number of characters in a voucher code (currently 5).
voucher-invalid-excluded-letters:
Error under the voucher code field instead of {{msg-proto|voucher-invalid}}, when a code that was not found contains I, L, O or U. Codes generated by the app never contain these letters because they are easily confused with the digits 1 and 0; codes the organizers made themselves may contain them, so this is only a hint. The typed text is kept in the field so it can be corrected.

I, L, O and U are the Latin letters as printed on the code; keep them as they are.
voucher-throttled:
Error under the voucher code field when too many wrong codes were entered recently, in this browser or on this consultation as a whole. Nothing is locked: once the wait is over, a valid code works again. Shown instead of {{msg-proto|voucher-invalid}}.

Parameters:
* $1 - number of seconds to wait before trying again.
voucher-invalid: Error under the voucher code field for a code that is wrong, revoked or expired. It is the same message for all of these on purpose, so it never reveals which applies.
voucher-already-joined: Error under the voucher code field when this browser is already signed in with a voucher account for the same consultation and a different, unused code is entered. The second code is not used.
voucher-switch-heading: Heading of the page shown before a voucher replaces the account already signed in in this browser (a Wikimedia account, or another voucher account). The body is {{msg-proto|voucher-switch-body}}; the buttons are {{msg-proto|voucher-switch-confirm}} and {{msg-proto|voucher-switch-cancel}}.
voucher-switch-confirm: Button under {{msg-proto|voucher-switch-body}} that signs out of the current account and continues with the voucher.
voucher-switch-cancel:
Link under {{msg-proto|voucher-switch-confirm}} that goes back to the consultation without changing accounts.
{{Identical|Cancel}}
